A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIC study by the same authors. The complete main texts and appendices A–E, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIC fine-tuning experiments, compositionality and downstream evaluations, and component, training-duration and encoder-freezing ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds authors-trained LLaVA comparisons, repeated-run measurements, long-caption retrieval and a manually assessed negative-generation experiment.

M1.justification: v2 adds a LLaVA adaptation pipeline that fine-tunes both CLIP encoders, transfers the vision encoder, and trains the projector and language model (Sections 4.5 and D.5). Appendix B.4 adds an LLM-guided negative-generation variant. Equation (5) also changes the stated loss aggregation. The original concatenation and alternating-update scheme remains; implementation changes for retained experiments are not established.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond the retained CLIP benchmarks to GQA, TextVQA, ScienceQA-Images and MME perception through LLaVA. It also adds qualitative open-ended captioning and a long-caption retrieval scenario using multiple sentences describing one scene. These substantially broaden task and input-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The original CLIP comparator sets are retained. New comparisons introduce an authors-trained standard LLaVA-1.5-7b control against its CLIC-equipped counterpart (Table 6), and an LLM SWAPS condition (Table 8). The earlier Non-random condition is retained as SAME NOUN, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: The new LLaVA experiment introduces 336×336 CLIP fine-tuning, an effective batch size of 40×8, staged projector/language-model training, matched baseline training and VQAScore evaluation. Long-caption retrieval introduces punctuation-based truncation within CLIP's 77-token context. These are added protocols; the original CLIP experiments retain their previously documented settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an LLM-swapping ablation and a manual quality audit of 75 negatives from each generation approach. Appendix E adds a long-caption test of concatenation shortcuts, success/failure cases across four SugarCrepe++ categories, and LLaVA captioning examples. The original component ablation is retained, moving from v1 Table 10 to v2 Table 4.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 Tables 10–11 introduce means and standard deviations over three independent runs for CLIC-LAION and CLIC-RedCaps across compositionality and downstream benchmarks. This establishes a substantial new reporting practice, although v1's unspecified run counts prevent claiming a particular increase in runs.

E6.justification: Matched original table values are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. v2 Table 6 reports WinoGround text scores of 36.7 versus 43.5 for CLIP-based versus CLIC-based LLaVA, while SQA-I scores are 69.2 versus 68.2. Additional results cover long-caption retrieval, repeated-run summaries, failure cases and negative quality: the manual audit reports 69% meaningful, grammatical negatives for LLM SWAPS versus 28% for standard CLIC.

T1.justification: Equation (5) moves the sum over four positive captions outside the logarithm: v1 takes the logarithm of summed positive-versus-negative probabilities, whereas v2 sums their logarithms. These expressions are not equivalent; v2 aligns with the stated per-positive penalty. This is a localized mathematical correction, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The original CLIP compositionality, retrieval and efficiency claims remain. v2 adds a third introductory contribution and a conclusion claim that CLIC vision features improve LLaVA compositional reasoning while preserving general VLM capabilities. This materially expands the claimed contribution beyond dual-encoder CLIP models.

C2.justification: v2 hypothesizes that reduced negative diversity explains the LLM-swapping variant's mixed results and interprets long-caption retrieval as evidence against concatenation shortcuts. Appendix A replaces v1's inability to test LLaVA with a limitation to the tested LLaVA setting. Figure 6 explicitly acknowledges persistent hallucinations in both LLaVA variants.

D1.justification: Section D.5 supplies model, dataset, resolution, batch size, training stages, baseline controls and codebase information for the new LLaVA pipeline. Appendix B.4 documents fine-grained POS processing, Gemini 2.5-Flash replacement candidates and preprocessing costs. Section D.1 also revises ambiguous GPU-hour wording to training durations on four A100 GPUs.

R1.justification: Eight targeted references are added, including Gemini 2.5, VQAScore, Long-CLIP and works supporting the new VQA evaluations. The established positioning against NegCLIP, DAC, SVLC and TripletCLIP remains substantially unchanged; the additions mainly contextualize the new experiments.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, expands explanatory examples in Appendix D.4, consolidates the former SOTA subsection into Section 4.4 and introduces dedicated LLaVA sections. Repetitive appendix ablation discussion is shortened, and front matter is updated. Most existing narrative and the appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds uncertainty tables, LLaVA and long-caption comparison tables, four illustrated success/failure tables with cosine scores, and a caption-response comparison figure. These substantially expand the visual evidence. The component ablation moves into the main text, while the original figures are retained and existing tables are redistributed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence by adding repeated-run uncertainty, direct tests of negative quality and concatenation shortcuts, and explicit failure examples. Its matched LLaVA experiment addresses v1's stated transfer limitation, while Equation (5) corrects an important specification error. These resolve meaningful reliability, applicability and documentation gaps. The gains remain qualified: LLaVA results lack repeated-run uncertainty, SQA-I decreases from 69.2 to 68.2, and captioning hallucinations persist.
